framework.name: Spring Boot
framework.tagline: The de-facto standard for production Java services.
framework.overview: Spring Boot builds on the Spring ecosystem with opinionated auto-configuration, embedded servers, and starter dependencies so you can ship REST APIs fast. Master it by climbing this ladder: expose an endpoint, inject collaborators, validate input, persist with JPA, handle errors globally, and lock behavior down with slice tests.

challenges.title: 1. First REST controller
challenges.concept: A `@RestController` maps HTTP requests to methods. `@GetMapping` binds a path, and the returned object is serialized to JSON automatically by Jackson.
steps: Read the name via @RequestParam with a default.
Return a record; Spring serializes it to JSON.
hints: A Java record makes a tidy response body.

challenges.title: 2. Dependency injection & service layer
challenges.concept: Keep controllers thin. Business logic lives in a `@Service` bean that Spring injects via constructor. Constructor injection keeps dependencies final and testable.
challenges.goal: Move greeting logic into a GreetingService and inject it into the controller.
steps: Create a @Service with a greet(name) method.
Declare it as a final field in the controller.
Delegate from the endpoint to the service.
hints: A single constructor is auto-wired; no @Autowired needed.

challenges.title: 3. Validate request bodies
challenges.concept: Use Bean Validation (`jakarta.validation`) with `@Valid` on the body. Invalid requests short-circuit with a 400 before your handler runs.
challenges.goal: Accept POST /users with a validated body {name, email}.
steps: Define a record with @NotBlank and @Email constraints.
hints: @Email on the email field, @NotBlank on name.
challenges.expectedOutput: POST /users with a blank name -> 400 Bad Request

challenges.title: 4. Persist with Spring Data JPA
challenges.concept: An `@Entity` maps to a table; a `JpaRepository` gives you CRUD plus derived query methods (like `findByEmail`) with zero SQL.
challenges.goal: Model a User entity and a repository with a findByEmail lookup.
steps: Annotate the class with @Entity and add an @Id @GeneratedValue field.
Add a derived query method Optional<User> findByEmail(String email).
hints: Spring implements the repository at runtime.
Method name maps to the WHERE clause.

challenges.title: 5. Global exception handling
challenges.concept: A `@RestControllerAdvice` centralizes error mapping. `@ExceptionHandler` methods translate exceptions into consistent JSON + status codes across every controller.
challenges.goal: Return 404 with a JSON body when a NotFoundException is thrown.

challenges.title: 6. Slice test with MockMvc
challenges.concept: `@WebMvcTest` loads only the web layer and gives you a `MockMvc` to drive requests without a running server. Collaborators are supplied as mocks so tests stay fast and focused.
challenges.goal: Assert GET /hello?name=Corgi returns 200 and the expected body.
hints: Use static imports from MockMvcRequestBuilders and MockMvcResultMatchers.
